title: PhysicsMaterialAPI
summary: Makes a prim a physics material and creates a PxMaterial for it. Enumerated by usd-schemas CONTAINS PhysicsMaterialAPI with physics:dynamicFriction as the probe column. Nothing here is units-scaled; the two friction defaults diverge from the raw schema fallback.
producer_scope: Every declared attribute is published at its resolved value, so an unauthored friction lands as the raw fallback 0.0 and a producer-populated stage never reaches the consumer's 0.5 defaults. No column is rewritten or created by the producer.

columns.name: physics:staticFriction
columns.absent: 0.5 (PhysX convention), not the schema fallback 0.0. Writing the raw fallback literally gives a frictionless material where an omitted column gives coefficient 0.5; USD population always publishes the resolved value, so an unauthored attribute yields 0.0 there.
columns.notes: Read without an authored gate: the column value always wins when present. No clamp; PhysX rejects negative values when the material is created.

columns.name: physics:dynamicFriction
columns.absent: 0.5, same divergence as physics:staticFriction: the raw fallback 0.0 is frictionless, the omitted column is 0.5.
columns.notes: Also the enumeration probe column: it is what materialises the matched prims in the walker.

verify.notes: Valid only while physxMaterial:compliantContactStiffness is 0. A positive compliant stiffness is stored by the consumer as a NEGATIVE restitution (setRestitution(-stiffness)), which overwrites this value in PhysX.

columns.name: physics:density
columns.absent: -1.0, the unset sentinel: mass computation ignores the material and falls back to PhysicsMassAPI density, then the consumer default density. The raw fallback 0.0 reads as unset too, so writing it literally is harmless.
columns.sentinel: -1.0; any value <= 0 is treated as unset by the mass computation, which uses a material density only when it is positive.
columns.notes: Not a PxMaterial property; it lives on the runtime's own material record and is consumed only by mass computation of shapes bound to this material. No PhysX getter, hence no verify block; it is observable indirectly through a bound body's mass.

interactions.rule: This API, not the prim type, is what physics enumerates. See Material for the consequences of a Material prim without it.
Combine modes and compliant contact live on PhysxMaterialAPI and are read only when that API is also in usd-schemas; without it every PhysX default applies (average combine, no compliance).
physics:density here is the second source of a shape's density, after an explicit PhysicsMassAPI density on the body and before the consumer default.

findings.summary: The consumer default 0.5 for both frictions disagrees with the schema fallback 0.0 that the producer publishes: a producer-populated Material simulates with friction 0, a hand-populated stage that omits the columns with 0.5. Observed in the material_bound_cube parity test (PxMaterial static friction 0.5 vs 0). Same for physics:dynamicFriction.
